title: Safehouse and Deadline
premise: Ivo Zhou, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group — an embassy that exists on no map and in no treaty — receives a call on a burner phone that was decommissioned years ago, from their former handler, Nadia, who officially died in a car bombing in Riga. Nadia warns that a staged infrastructure disaster, designed to look like an accident and pinned on a scapegoated diaspora community, is scheduled for the Meridian Summit in eleven days, and that someone inside Ivo's own organization greenlit it. As Ivo assembles an unlikely crew of exiles, burned assets, and one terrified analyst, they discover the attack is a loyalty test: whoever stops it proves themselves disposable; whoever lets it happen inherits the machine. In the end Ivo chooses the crew over the institution, exposing the plot publicly at the cost of their cover, their country's protection, and any chance of going home — but gaining, for the first time, people who chose them back.
about_author: Yara Fairweather is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent six years writing risk assessments for organizations she can't name, before trading classified memos for fiction. She writes thrillers about people who do the quiet, deniable work of governments — and what it costs them to stay human.

chapters.title: The Phone That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ivo Zhou's POV. On a routine errand in Vienna, Ivo finds a burner phone sewn into the lining of a coat they're returning to a dead drop — a model discontinued after the Riga operation. That night it rings. The voice is Nadia's, and Nadia has been dead for three years. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread as old grief is weaponized.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rules
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with flashbacks to recruitment. Ivo reports the call through proper channels and is told, gently and firmly, to destroy the phone and take scheduled leave. The institutional warmth feels rehearsed. Alone, Ivo replays the voiceprint against memory and finds it matches. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life built entirely inside an organization that just asked them to ignore a ghost.

chapters.title: Dead Woman Dialing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ivo and the caller. The phone rings again; 'Nadia' gives a date, a target — the Meridian Summit's transit hub — and a phrase only Nadia knew. Ivo traces the signal to a relay in Trieste and realizes the caller knows Ivo's movements in real time. Emotional beat: paranoia braided with longing; the first crack in Ivo's loyalty.

chapters.title: The Scapegoat File
chapters.summary: Ivo breaks into the Group's Vienna annex archive. They find a contingency plan, COLD HARBOR: a manufactured transit disaster attributed to a diaspora community, complete with pre-written attribution dossiers dated next week. Someone has already written the ending. Emotional beat: cold horror giving way to fury.

chapters.title: Leave of Absence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Officially on leave, Ivo burns twelve years of careful anonymity in forty-eight hours: cashing favors, buying untraceable gear, contacting Tomas Reyes, a burned signals analyst living under another man's name in Porto. Tomas refuses — then finds his own name in COLD HARBOR's witness list. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into commitment; the found family begins to gather.

chapters.title: Porto, Rain, and Old Debts
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas and Ivo reconstruct how the attack will be staged: a maintenance override, a pressure fault, plausible deniability engineered by someone with root access to the Group itself. Tomas insists they need eyes inside — which means Amara Sesay, an asset Ivo once abandoned in Lagos. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing; Ivo must ask forgiveness from someone they sacrificed.

chapters.title: Amara Sesay Says No
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara, now running a legitimate logistics firm, listens to Ivo's apology and pitch and throws them out. But alone, she pulls her own surveillance sweep logs and finds a Meridian Group shadow contract routed through her company without her knowledge. She calls Ivo back at 3 a.m.: 'I'm not doing this for you.' Emotional beat: wounded pride hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Root Access
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Inside the shadow contract, Tomas finds the operational signature of Deputy Director Halloran — Ivo's mentor, the man who recruited them. Ivo refuses to believe it and flies to confront Halloran personally, off-book. Emotional beat: denial as self-protection; the mentor myth beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Garden
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Over tea in Halloran's Oxford garden, Ivo probes; Halloran deflects beautifully, then says one sentence too precise about the Summit's transit hub. He knows what Ivo knows. Walking away, Ivo spots the counter-surveillance team he assigned to protect them. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The team convenes in a Lisbon safehouse — Ivo, Tomas, Amara, and Dov, a paranoid ex-Group courier who arrives with the physical keys to the transit hub's maintenance network. They map the attack window: nine days, during a scheduled 'drill' that will empty the real responders. Emotional beat: cautious camaraderie; the safehouse starts feeling like a home none of them expected.

chapters.title: What Nadia Knew
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the burner's breadcrumbs to a Riga storage unit, Ivo finds Nadia's real effects — and evidence she discovered COLD HARBOR before her death, meaning the car bomb wasn't an accident. The caller isn't Nadia; it's someone using her archive. Emotional beat: grief recontextualized; mourning becomes motive.

chapters.title: The Voice Behind the Voice
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Voice analysis reveals the caller: Lena Voss, Nadia's protégé, presumed dead in the same bombing — alive, radicalized, and planning to stop COLD HARBOR by any means, including detonating early to force evacuation and martyrdom for the blamed community. Stopping the attack means stopping her too. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; ally and threat in one body.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo meets Voss in a Tallinn chapel. She offers proof of Halloran's chain of command in exchange for Ivo helping her expose everything — even if exposure kills hundreds in the chaos. Ivo counters: help us stop it cleanly, and we burn the Group together. Uneasy truce. Emotional beat: negotiation between vengeance and conscience.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The Group notices the leaks. A cleanup team hits the Lisbon safehouse while the crew is out; Dov is taken. Halloran sends Ivo a personal message: come home, and everyone walks. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness — the found family realizes it has become leverage.

chapters.title: Trading Dov
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo offers Halloran a trade: Dov for the COLD HARBOR master key, staged through Amara's logistics network. The exchange works — too smoothly. Tomas discovers the returned Dov carries a tracker, and the drill schedule has moved up: five days now. Emotional beat: relief curdling into the realization they were never negotiating as equals.

chapters.title: Five Days, One Plan
chapters.summary: Full-crew POV rotation. The plan: Amara's firm wins the emergency maintenance contract (legitimately, barely), Tomas inserts the override kill-switch, Dov maps guard rotations, Ivo gets Voss to stand down her parallel detonation. Every piece requires trust between people with every reason to betray each other. Emotional beat: fragile unity forged under deadline.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. The tracker wasn't passive — it fed the Group their plan. Dov confesses he suspected and said nothing, ashamed. With hours left, the crew rebuilds the approach around the compromised route, turning the leak into bait. Emotional beat: shame met with grace; belonging chosen despite failure.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Final preparations. Halloran calls Ivo directly: he knows about Voss, about all of them, and offers Ivo Nadia's real file — the truth of her death — if Ivo stands down tonight. Ivo asks one question: 'Did you order Riga?' His silence answers. Emotional beat: the last tie to the old life severed deliberately.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax, part one. The drill empties the hub; Voss arms her device as leverage; Tomas fights the Group's counter-override; Amara locks down the maintenance network. Ivo reaches Voss in the service tunnels and talks her down from detonation by promising the exposure she actually wants — names, documents, broadcast. Emotional beat: maximum tension resolving not through force but through being believed.

chapters.title: COLD HARBOR, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax, part two. The kill-switch holds; the 'accident' never happens; Voss surrenders her device to Ivo rather than the Group. But Halloran triggers the fallback: pin the foiled plot on the crew itself. As arrest teams close in, Ivo executes the endgame — streaming the COLD HARBOR dossier, the Riga evidence, and Halloran's authorization live. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unofficial
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Halloran is arrested by his own institution to contain the damage; the Group survives, smaller and warier. Voss turns herself in, naming names. Ivo is officially erased — no protection, no pension, no country. The crew regroups in the Lisbon safehouse, now just an apartment with bad plumbing and good coffee. Emotional beat: loss and lightness coexisting.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. Months later, the four run a small, honest private-intelligence practice out of the apartment. A new burner phone arrives in the mail; Ivo drops it in the harbor without answering. On the balcony, Tomas asks if Ivo regrets it. Ivo watches Amara and Dov argue about dinner and says no. Emotional beat: quiet arrival — belonging, finally, at the price of everything else, and worth it.
